title: Vademecum of the GPAI Signatory Taskforce

policy_extraction.issuing_body: European AI Office and Signatories to the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
covered_actors: Signatories to the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (Taskforce Members)
General-purpose AI model providers participating as Signatories

evidence.quote: Having regard to the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice published on 10 July 2025 (the ‘Code’), assessed as adequate pursuant to Article 56(6) AI Act, this Vademecum sets out the organisation and operation of the Signatory Taskforce (the ‘Taskforce’)

The objectives of the Taskforce are, inter alia:
(a) to facilitate cooperation between Signatories where relevant for the purpose of implementing the Code;

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Operational vademecum setting out the governance, membership, objectives, ad hoc groups, meeting procedures (at least yearly), consensus decision-making (minimum 10 working days for objections), stakeholder invitations, and confidentiality rules of the Signatory Taskforce for the EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (published 10 July 2025 and assessed as adequate under Article 56(6) AI Act). Participation is opt-in and Members may join or withdraw at any time; Members must comply with applicable EU law, notably competition rules, during Taskforce activities. Lists 24 participating signatory organisations.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: This Vademecum is predominantly a procedural and organizational document establishing the rules of operation, membership, meetings, decision-making, and confidentiality for the Signatory Taskforce of the EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice, and therefore contains very limited explicit risk-framing language. To the extent a governance rationale is articulated in Point 2 (Objectives), it centers on agile, collaborative, and adaptive implementation of the voluntary Code through signatory cooperation, stakeholder exchanges, and updating guidance documents in light of technological, societal, market, and legislative developments—aligning modestly with innovation_enablement. Although the text briefly references 'changes in the risk landscape' and 'societal' and 'market' developments, it makes no explicit substantive appeals to fundamental rights, consumer/public safety harms, catastrophic risks, national security, international economic competitiveness, social stability, or labor transition.

evidence_spans.quote: (c) to exchange views on technological developments, changes in the risk landscape, or experience with the application of the AI Act rules that could be relevant for potential future reviews or updates of the Code, without prejudice to the necessary public consultations by the AI Office on any such possible updates;
